I added `Money.apply_rate(rate: Decimal) -> Money` in `ledger/money.py`, and all 10 tests pass.

It multiplies the cents by `rate` using `Decimal`, so no float is involved. It then rounds to the nearest cent with `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

The rules in `money.py` already say rate math must round half-up, not banker's, and must not go through float. I followed them as written, so no rule, test or other code needed changing.

Half-cents round away from zero, so negative amounts mirror positive ones. For example, 2.50 at rate 0.01 gives 0.03, and -2.50 gives -0.03.

I didn't add a dedicated test for `apply_rate`; I only spot-checked those values by hand.
